content.name: Festival National des Arts et de la Culture (FENAC)

attributes.description: A national festival of Cameroonian arts, music and dance, described as the largest in the country with no religious affiliation.
attributes.activities: Parades, music and dance shows, storytelling, traditional games and food, and promotion of indigenous languages and heritage.
attributes.place: One travel guide places it in Maroua in December, while another says it rotates across the major cities.
attributes.caution: Sources differ on where and when it is held.

content.name: Abine-mfor and Mandeleh festivals of Bafut

attributes.place: Bafut Palace, the royal residence of the Fon of Bafut, in the Northwest Region.
attributes.abine_mfor: Means dance of the Fon in the Bafut language, and is also called Abine Lela, the flutes' dance.
attributes.purpose: The Bafut people perform traditional rituals to honour ancestral spirits, reflecting their religious and political beliefs.
attributes.timing: One charity blog says the Fon dance is held every December and has been held every year since 1516, which I could not verify.
attributes.palace: The same blog calls Bafut Palace the centre of the region's politics and religious rites for over 400 years.
attributes.mandeleh: A second major annual festival held at the palace.

source.citation: Basel Mission Archives photographs of the Lela festival at Bali (1908 to 1911), and the Technium paper on Abine Lela. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.history: The Lela festival was already being photographed in Bali by Basel Mission photographers between 1908 and 1911, in images such as King Fo Nyonga at the Lela dance and a parade during the Lela festival.
attributes.note: Bafut's flute dance is also called Abine Lela, so check which Lela a source means.
